questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.1.1: Design and configure mechanisms to require encryption when connecting to resources.
questions.text: A public ALB must reject clients that use obsolete TLS versions while preserving HTTPS for modern browsers. What should the security engineer configure?

answers.text: An ELB security policy that permits only approved TLS versions and ciphers
An S3 Lifecycle rule on access logs
An IAM password policy for application users
EBS encryption on the load balancer targets only

explanations.a: ELB security policies define the TLS protocol and cipher suites used by HTTPS listeners.
explanations.b: For encryption in transit enforcement, lifecycle rules manage object retention and do not control TLS negotiation.
explanations.c: This is negotiated by network endpoints, not by console password rules.
explanations.d: At-rest volume encryption does not require clients to use modern TLS.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.1.1: Design and configure mechanisms to require encryption when connecting to resources.
questions.text: A compliance requirement states that all connections to an Amazon RDS database must use TLS. What should be implemented?

answers.text: Use public subnets for the database
Require SSL or TLS at the database layer and distribute the correct trust bundle to clients
Enable S3 Object Lock on database exports only
Increase the database backup retention period

explanations.a: This approach is not achieved by public subnet placement and would increase exposure.
explanations.b: Database-side TLS enforcement and trusted certificates ensure clients establish encrypted database sessions.
explanations.c: Object Lock protects stored objects and does not force live RDS connections to use TLS.
explanations.d: Backup retention does not affect whether current client connections are encrypted.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.1.1: Design and configure mechanisms to require encryption when connecting to resources.
questions.text: A CloudFront distribution serves an API. The company requires viewers to use HTTPS and origins to receive encrypted traffic. What configuration satisfies this?

answers.text: Use a wider cache TTL for API responses
Store API logs in an encrypted bucket only
Set viewer protocol policy to redirect or require HTTPS and use HTTPS-only origin protocol policy
Use an IAM permissions boundary on the distribution owner

explanations.a: Cache TTL affects content freshness and does not enforce TLS on either connection leg.
explanations.b: Encrypted log storage does not require encrypted viewer or origin transport.
explanations.c: CloudFront can enforce HTTPS from viewers and use encrypted connections to origins.
explanations.d: Permissions boundaries limit IAM permissions and do not configure CloudFront protocol policy.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.1.1: Design and configure mechanisms to require encryption when connecting to resources.
questions.text: A private API endpoint must be accessible only with TLS 1.2 or later. Which control should be selected?

answers.text: Enable DynamoDB point-in-time recovery
Use a NAT gateway for inbound API traffic
Change the API stage description
Configure the API's custom domain or fronting load balancer with an approved TLS security policy

explanations.a: PITR protects table recovery and does not reject older TLS clients.
explanations.b: NAT gateways are not inbound API TLS termination points.
explanations.c: Descriptions are metadata and do not enforce TLS versions.
explanations.d: The TLS policy on the serving endpoint determines which client protocol versions are accepted.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.1.1: Design and configure mechanisms to require encryption when connecting to resources.
questions.text: A company wants end users to know they are connecting to the intended public application domain. What data-in-transit control is required?

answers.text: A trusted public certificate on the HTTPS endpoint that matches the application domain
A private AMI hardened with CIS settings
An SQS dead-letter queue for failed events
A KMS key alias that matches the DNS name

explanations.a: A valid certificate lets clients authenticate the endpoint and establish an encrypted session.
explanations.b: Host hardening supports compute security but does not prove the public domain identity to browsers.
explanations.c: Dead-letter queues preserve failed messages and do not provide endpoint identity.
explanations.d: A key alias does not authenticate a public TLS endpoint to clients.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.1.1: Design and configure mechanisms to require encryption when connecting to resources.
questions.text: An ALB listener supports TLS, but scanners report weak ciphers. What should be changed?

answers.text: Rotate the application database password
Select a stronger ELB security policy that removes the weak cipher suites
Add more target group health checks
Enable EFS lifecycle policies

explanations.a: Credential rotation does not change the cipher suites offered by the ALB.
explanations.b: The listener's security policy controls which cipher suites the ALB offers during TLS negotiation.
explanations.c: Health checks do not modify TLS cipher selection.
explanations.d: EFS lifecycle management does not harden ALB TLS settings.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.1.1: Design and configure mechanisms to require encryption when connecting to resources.
questions.text: An application sends customer data to an external partner API. The security team requires encryption and server identity validation. What should the client verify?

answers.text: Only the HTTP response body length
Only the local instance profile name
The partner endpoint certificate chain and hostname during TLS negotiation
Only the S3 storage class of archived payloads

explanations.a: Body length does not prove the partner endpoint identity or TLS trust.
explanations.b: Instance profile names do not validate a remote TLS certificate.
explanations.c: Client-side certificate validation prevents encrypted connections to an untrusted or impersonated endpoint.
explanations.d: Storage class does not secure live partner API connections.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.1.1: Design and configure mechanisms to require encryption when connecting to resources.
questions.text: A team wants to prevent accidental plaintext access to an S3 bucket. What bucket policy condition can help?

answers.text: Deny requests when object tags are missing only
Allow all requests from any source IP
Use S3 Lifecycle expiration for noncurrent versions
Deny requests when aws:SecureTransport is false

explanations.a: Tag enforcement can support governance but does not specifically block plaintext transport.
explanations.b: Broad allowance would not enforce encrypted transport.
explanations.c: Lifecycle expiration does not distinguish HTTPS from HTTP requests.
explanations.d: The aws:SecureTransport condition can block non-TLS requests to S3 resources.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.1.1: Design and configure mechanisms to require encryption when connecting to resources.
questions.text: A service mesh in Kubernetes must encrypt service-to-service calls between pods. Which control aligns with the requirement?

answers.text: Use mutual TLS between services with managed certificate rotation
Use only Kubernetes labels for encryption status
Store pod logs in CloudWatch Logs
Enable node volume encryption only

explanations.a: Mutual TLS encrypts traffic and authenticates services on both sides of the connection.
explanations.b: Labels can mark intent but do not encrypt network traffic.
explanations.c: Central logging does not encrypt live pod-to-pod communication.
explanations.d: Node storage encryption protects data at rest and not traffic between services.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.1.2: Design and configure mechanisms for secure and private access to resources.
questions.text: A private application must consume an AWS service without traversing the public internet. What should be configured?

answers.text: A public NAT gateway route to every service
A VPC endpoint with appropriate endpoint policy and private DNS settings
An open security group on the application
A bucket lifecycle policy

explanations.a: Avoids unnecessary public paths when private endpoints are required.
explanations.b: VPC endpoints provide private connectivity to supported AWS services and can be scoped by policy.
explanations.c: Broad network access weakens secure private resource access.
explanations.d: Lifecycle policies manage stored objects and do not create private service connectivity.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.1.2: Design and configure mechanisms for secure and private access to resources.
questions.text: A partner needs access to one internal service without broad network access to the VPC. Which design is appropriate?

answers.text: Full VPC peering with all route tables propagated
Publicly route the service through an internet gateway
Expose the service through AWS PrivateLink
Share application administrator credentials with the partner

explanations.a: Full network peering can expose more resources than the partner needs.
explanations.b: Public routing conflicts with secure private resource access.
explanations.c: PrivateLink offers service-scoped private connectivity without exposing the full VPC network.
explanations.d: Credentials are not a private network connectivity pattern.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.1.2: Design and configure mechanisms for secure and private access to resources.
questions.text: Remote employees need private access to AWS resources with device and identity context. Which service is relevant?

answers.text: S3 Object Lock
Amazon Inspector image scanning
AWS Backup copy jobs
AWS Verified Access

explanations.a: Object retention does not provide user-to-application private access.
explanations.b: Image scanning does not authenticate remote employees to private resources.
explanations.c: Backup copies do not create private employee access.
explanations.d: Verified Access evaluates identity and device trust signals before granting access to private applications.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.1.2: Design and configure mechanisms for secure and private access to resources.
questions.text: A developer needs encrypted access from a laptop to private VPC resources. Which option is suitable?

answers.text: AWS Client VPN with authentication and authorization controls
Public SSH to every private instance
A CloudFront cache behavior for database traffic
An IAM access key embedded in the laptop browser

explanations.a: Client VPN provides managed VPN access into VPC resources using approved identity controls.
explanations.b: Opening direct SSH broadly increases exposure and does not provide managed private access.
explanations.c: CloudFront cache behavior is not a private database access method.
explanations.d: Access keys do not create private network connectivity.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.1.2: Design and configure mechanisms for secure and private access to resources.
questions.text: A workload reaches S3 through a gateway endpoint, but it can access buckets outside the approved data account. What should be tightened?

answers.text: The ALB target response timeout
The VPC endpoint policy and bucket policies for the intended resources
The EC2 AMI description
The SNS topic display name

explanations.a: Load balancer timeout does not scope S3 private access.
explanations.b: Endpoint and resource policies can limit which buckets and principals use the private path.
explanations.c: AMI descriptions do not restrict endpoint access.
explanations.d: Topic names do not limit S3 endpoint reachability.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.1.2: Design and configure mechanisms for secure and private access to resources.
questions.text: A company uses interface endpoints for private API access. DNS resolves to public IPs from inside the VPC. What should be checked?

answers.text: Only the EBS snapshot schedule
Only the IAM password policy
Private DNS configuration and resolver behavior for the endpoint
Only the S3 object lock mode

explanations.a: Snapshot timing does not affect endpoint DNS resolution.
explanations.b: Password policy does not direct DNS to interface endpoints.
explanations.c: Specifically, Secure private resource access often depends on DNS resolving service names to private endpoint addresses.
explanations.d: Object retention mode does not configure private DNS.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.1.2: Design and configure mechanisms for secure and private access to resources.
questions.text: A SaaS provider exposes a service through PrivateLink. The consumer wants to restrict which principals can connect. What should be used?

answers.text: A public DNS record that bypasses PrivateLink
A shared root user in the provider account
A CloudWatch dashboard widget
Endpoint service permissions and endpoint policies where applicable

explanations.a: Public DNS bypasses the intended private access path.
explanations.b: Root credentials are not needed for endpoint authorization.
explanations.c: Dashboard widgets do not grant or deny endpoint connectivity.
explanations.d: PrivateLink connections should be authorized to approved consumers and constrained by policies.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.1.2: Design and configure mechanisms for secure and private access to resources.
questions.text: A team wants private access to an application without routing users onto the entire corporate network. Which pattern fits?

answers.text: Identity-aware application access through Verified Access
A full-mesh VPN for every user to every subnet
Public access with an obscure URL
Unrestricted inbound rules on private subnets

explanations.a: Verified Access can grant application-specific access without broad network-level VPN reachability.
explanations.b: Broad network access can violate least-privilege connectivity goals.
explanations.c: Obscurity does not provide secure private resource access.
explanations.d: Unrestricted inbound access undermines private application protection.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.1.2: Design and configure mechanisms for secure and private access to resources.
questions.text: A security engineer is troubleshooting a VPC endpoint access failure. What should be reviewed?

answers.text: Only the Lambda function memory size
Route tables, security groups for interface endpoints, endpoint policy, resource policy, and DNS
Only the cost allocation tag values
Only the CloudFront viewer protocol policy

explanations.a: Function memory does not determine endpoint network or policy access.
explanations.b: Endpoint access depends on both network path and authorization controls.
explanations.c: Cost tags do not authorize private endpoint use.
explanations.d: Viewer protocol settings do not troubleshoot VPC endpoint access.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.1.3: Design and configure inter-resource encryption in transit.
questions.text: An Amazon EMR cluster processes regulated data. The requirement is to encrypt traffic between cluster nodes. What should be enabled?

answers.text: Only S3 bucket versioning for EMR output
Only a public subnet for every EMR node
EMR in-transit encryption in the security configuration
Only IAM user MFA for cluster operators

explanations.a: Versioning protects object history but does not encrypt node-to-node traffic.
explanations.b: Public subnet placement does not provide inter-resource encryption in transit.
explanations.c: EMR security configurations can require encryption for traffic between cluster components.
explanations.d: Operator MFA does not encrypt traffic inside the cluster.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.1.3: Design and configure inter-resource encryption in transit.
questions.text: An EKS workload requires encrypted communication between services in the cluster. Which design should be considered?

answers.text: Only EBS encryption for worker nodes
Only Kubernetes namespace names
Only image tag immutability
Mutual TLS through a service mesh or application-level TLS between services

explanations.a: Volume encryption protects stored data and not service-to-service traffic.
explanations.b: Namespaces organize resources but do not encrypt traffic.
explanations.c: Tag immutability protects image references and not runtime network traffic.
explanations.d: Specifically, Inter-resource encryption in transit requires the communicating services to establish encrypted sessions.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.1.3: Design and configure inter-resource encryption in transit.
questions.text: A SageMaker AI notebook accesses a model endpoint and sensitive training data. What should be required?

answers.text: TLS connections and private network paths where applicable between notebook, endpoint, and data services
Public access to every training artifact
Only local notebook comments that mention encryption
Only disabling CloudWatch logging

explanations.a: SageMaker AI workflows should protect data movement between resources with encrypted transport and private access when required.
explanations.b: Public artifacts conflict with protecting sensitive data movement.
explanations.c: Comments do not enforce encrypted transport.
explanations.d: Removing logs does not protect inter-resource communication.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.1.3: Design and configure inter-resource encryption in transit.
questions.text: A Nitro-based EC2 workload handles sensitive traffic between instances in the same VPC. What should the architect understand?

answers.text: Nitro encryption replaces all application TLS requirements
Nitro-based instances can provide encryption in transit for supported instance-to-instance traffic, but requirements must be validated for the workload path
Nitro disables the need for network segmentation
Nitro automatically encrypts all internet traffic end to end

explanations.a: Workload and compliance needs may still require TLS at application or service layers.
explanations.b: Inter-resource encryption in transit depends on supported instance types, paths, and service behavior.
explanations.c: Encryption does not replace network access controls.
explanations.d: Internet paths include external hops outside the EC2 Nitro domain.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.1.3: Design and configure inter-resource encryption in transit.
questions.text: A distributed database cluster needs encrypted internode replication. What should be configured?

answers.text: An S3 lifecycle transition for database backups
An IAM policy name containing TLS
The database engine or service setting for TLS or internode encryption
A CloudFront distribution in front of the database

explanations.a: Backup lifecycle does not encrypt live replication traffic.
explanations.b: Policy names do not enable database internode encryption.
explanations.c: Replication traffic must be encrypted by the service or engine that performs the node-to-node communication.
explanations.d: CloudFront is not the control for database node replication.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.1.3: Design and configure inter-resource encryption in transit.
questions.text: A workload uses AWS service calls from Lambda to DynamoDB. What protects data in transit for the service API call?

answers.text: DynamoDB TTL on items
Lambda reserved concurrency
A longer function description
HTTPS to the AWS service endpoint with certificate validation

explanations.a: TTL expires items and does not secure API transport.
explanations.b: Concurrency limits do not encrypt network communication.
explanations.c: Descriptions do not affect TLS use.
explanations.d: AWS service API calls use TLS endpoints, and clients must validate the service certificate chain.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.1.3: Design and configure inter-resource encryption in transit.
questions.text: A containerized microservice connects to an internal Redis-compatible cache. The cache supports TLS but clients use plaintext. What should be remediated?

answers.text: Enable TLS on the cache endpoint and update client connection configuration
Increase pod replica count
Archive cache logs to Glacier only
Rename the service to secure-cache

explanations.a: Both server-side TLS support and client-side TLS settings are required for encrypted cache sessions.
explanations.b: More pods do not change plaintext cache communication.
explanations.c: Archived logs do not encrypt current cache traffic.
explanations.d: Names do not enforce transport encryption.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.1.3: Design and configure inter-resource encryption in transit.
questions.text: An internal gRPC service requires authenticated encryption between workloads. Which pattern fits?

answers.text: Plain HTTP with a custom header named encrypted
mTLS with workload identities and certificate rotation
Only subnet isolation with no TLS
Only object versioning for request payloads

explanations.a: A header name does not encrypt or authenticate the connection.
explanations.b: Mutual TLS authenticates both services and encrypts the gRPC connection.
explanations.c: Network isolation helps but does not provide encrypted service-to-service communication.
explanations.d: Object versioning does not protect live gRPC traffic.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.1.3: Design and configure inter-resource encryption in transit.
questions.text: A security reviewer asks how to prove inter-resource encryption is active. What evidence is useful?

answers.text: Only the number of resources in the VPC
Only the account's billing contacts
Service configuration, client connection settings, certificate state, and test results from representative paths
Only the color of a network diagram

explanations.a: Resource count does not prove encrypted connections.
explanations.b: Billing metadata does not validate transport security.
explanations.c: Inter-resource encryption needs evidence that both endpoints are configured and actual connections negotiate encryption.
explanations.d: Diagram styling is not evidence of encryption enforcement.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.1: Design, implement, and configure data encryption at rest based on specific requirements.
questions.text: A database contains regulated records and must use keys that the customer controls and can audit. Which encryption-at-rest option fits?

answers.text: Store records unencrypted because the database is private
Use only TLS for database clients
Rely on database name prefixes for protection
Enable service encryption with a customer managed AWS KMS key

explanations.a: Private networking does not replace data encryption at rest.
explanations.b: TLS protects data in transit and not stored database files.
explanations.c: Naming conventions do not encrypt stored data.
explanations.d: Customer managed KMS keys provide AWS-managed service integration with customer-controlled policies and audit visibility.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.1: Design, implement, and configure data encryption at rest based on specific requirements.
questions.text: A workload requires dedicated HSM control for cryptographic keys instead of shared KMS key storage. Which service should be selected?

answers.text: AWS CloudHSM
AWS WAF
Amazon SQS
AWS Backup Vault Lock

explanations.a: CloudHSM provides dedicated hardware security modules for workloads that require direct HSM control.
explanations.b: WAF filters web requests and does not store encryption keys for data at rest.
explanations.c: SQS queues messages and does not provide dedicated HSMs.
explanations.d: Vault Lock protects backup retention and does not provide HSM key custody.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.1: Design, implement, and configure data encryption at rest based on specific requirements.
questions.text: An application must encrypt data before sending it to S3, and AWS must not see plaintext. Which pattern fits?

answers.text: S3 server-side encryption only
Client-side encryption before upload
S3 public access blocks only
CloudFront signed URLs only

explanations.a: Server-side encryption encrypts after S3 receives the data and does not meet client-side plaintext control.
explanations.b: Client-side encryption protects data before it reaches the storage service.
explanations.c: Public access controls do not encrypt object contents before upload.
explanations.d: Signed URLs control access and do not perform client-side encryption.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.1: Design, implement, and configure data encryption at rest based on specific requirements.
questions.text: A new EBS volume must be encrypted automatically in every Region used by the account. What should be configured?

answers.text: An IAM password policy
A CloudWatch dashboard for volume count
EBS encryption by default in each required Region
An S3 CORS rule

explanations.a: Password policy does not encrypt block storage.
explanations.b: A dashboard can show resources but does not enforce encryption.
explanations.c: EBS encryption defaults ensure new supported volumes are encrypted without relying on manual selection.
explanations.d: CORS affects browser access to S3 and not EBS encryption.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.1: Design, implement, and configure data encryption at rest based on specific requirements.
questions.text: A company uses Amazon EFS for shared files and must encrypt stored data. What should be enabled?

answers.text: Only NACL rules on mount targets
Only DNS private hosted zones
Only application debug logging
EFS encryption at rest with an AWS KMS key

explanations.a: Network ACLs filter traffic and do not encrypt stored EFS data.
explanations.b: DNS resolution does not encrypt file system storage.
explanations.c: Debug logs do not protect stored files.
explanations.d: EFS supports encryption at rest using KMS keys to protect file system data.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.1: Design, implement, and configure data encryption at rest based on specific requirements.
questions.text: A multi-tenant application stores encrypted objects in S3 and wants tenant separation in key usage. What design should be considered?

answers.text: Use separate KMS keys or encryption context controls aligned to tenant isolation requirements
One public KMS key policy for every tenant
Disable object encryption and rely on bucket names
Use the same unrestricted decrypt role for all tenants

explanations.a: Tenant-sensitive encryption design can use key separation and encryption context to support audit and access boundaries.
explanations.b: Public decrypt access would break tenant confidentiality.
explanations.c: Bucket names do not protect object contents.
explanations.d: A single broad decrypt role weakens tenant isolation.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.1: Design, implement, and configure data encryption at rest based on specific requirements.
questions.text: A data lake stores objects encrypted with SSE-S3, but auditors require customer control over key policies. What should be changed?

answers.text: Remove encryption because S3 is durable
Use SSE-KMS with customer managed KMS keys
Use only S3 Versioning
Use only lifecycle transitions to colder storage

explanations.a: Durability does not provide confidentiality.
explanations.b: SSE-KMS with customer managed keys provides key policy control and KMS audit events.
explanations.c: Versioning protects object history and not key policy control.
explanations.d: Storage class transitions do not satisfy customer key policy requirements.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.1: Design, implement, and configure data encryption at rest based on specific requirements.
questions.text: A service needs to decrypt data in one account with a KMS key in another account. What must be configured?

answers.text: Only a VPC peering connection
Only a matching alias name in both accounts
Key policy and IAM permissions that allow the approved cross-account principal to use the key
Only S3 Transfer Acceleration

explanations.a: Network peering does not grant KMS decrypt permission.
explanations.b: Aliases do not establish cross-account key trust.
explanations.c: Cross-account KMS use requires authorization on the key and permissions for the caller.
explanations.d: Transfer acceleration does not authorize KMS use.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.1: Design, implement, and configure data encryption at rest based on specific requirements.
questions.text: A regulated workload needs proof that encryption at rest is consistently enabled. What evidence should be collected?

answers.text: Only a verbal statement from the application owner
Only the number of subnets
Only front-end TLS certificates
AWS Config evaluations, service encryption settings, KMS key policies, and CloudTrail KMS events

explanations.a: Verbal confirmation is weak evidence for encryption compliance.
explanations.b: Subnet count does not prove stored data encryption.
explanations.c: TLS certificates protect transport and do not prove data at rest is encrypted.
explanations.d: Encryption-at-rest evidence should show configuration state, key governance, and cryptographic use activity.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.2: Design and configure mechanisms to protect data integrity.
questions.text: A financial archive in S3 must prevent object deletion or overwrite during a regulatory retention period. Which feature should be used?

answers.text: S3 Object Lock in the required retention mode
S3 Transfer Acceleration
CloudFront signed cookies
IAM password rotation

explanations.a: S3 Object Lock provides write-once-read-many controls that protect object integrity during retention.
explanations.b: Transfer Acceleration improves network transfer performance and does not prevent deletion.
explanations.c: Signed cookies control viewer access and not archive integrity.
explanations.d: Password rotation does not lock stored S3 objects.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.2: Design and configure mechanisms to protect data integrity.
questions.text: A company wants to preserve previous versions of objects when accidental overwrites occur. What should be enabled?

answers.text: S3 CORS with wildcard origins
S3 Versioning
VPC Flow Logs
ALB stickiness

explanations.a: CORS controls browser access and does not preserve previous object versions.
explanations.b: Versioning keeps multiple object versions so prior data can be restored after overwrite or deletion markers.
explanations.c: Flow logs capture network metadata and not object history.
explanations.d: Stickiness affects request routing and not object integrity.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.2: Design and configure mechanisms to protect data integrity.
questions.text: A Glacier vault must enforce a retention policy that administrators cannot relax. Which control applies?

answers.text: CloudWatch metric math
Amazon Cognito passwordless sign-in
S3 Glacier Vault Lock
AWS WAF bot rules

explanations.a: Metric math analyzes metrics and does not enforce archive retention.
explanations.b: Authentication features do not lock Glacier vault policies.
explanations.c: Vault Lock can enforce compliance controls for vault archives according to a locked policy.
explanations.d: WAF rules protect web applications and not archive retention.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.2: Design and configure mechanisms to protect data integrity.
questions.text: A software release package must be validated before deployment to production. What integrity control should be used?

answers.text: Increasing the artifact bucket TTL
Using only file names that include trusted
Disabling deployment logs
Digital code signing and signature verification in the deployment pipeline

explanations.a: Object retention timing does not prove package authenticity.
explanations.b: Names do not cryptographically validate integrity.
explanations.c: Removing logs weakens auditability and does not validate artifacts.
explanations.d: Code signing verifies that the artifact is trusted and has not been altered before deployment.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.2: Design and configure mechanisms to protect data integrity.
questions.text: A team downloads sensitive files from S3 and must detect corruption or tampering after transfer. What should be verified?

answers.text: Checksums or cryptographic hashes compared with trusted values
Only the downloader's IAM user name
Only the bucket storage class
Only object key length

explanations.a: Checksum or hash validation can detect whether file contents changed during storage or transfer.
explanations.b: Identity context does not prove file contents are unchanged.
explanations.c: Storage class does not validate content integrity.
explanations.d: Key length does not prove file integrity.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.2: Design and configure mechanisms to protect data integrity.
questions.text: A backup bucket uses Object Lock, but a lifecycle policy is set to expire objects early. What should the engineer confirm?

answers.text: Lifecycle always overrides Object Lock
Locked retention prevents deletion before the retention date for protected versions
Object Lock makes encryption unnecessary
Object Lock changes object contents automatically

explanations.a: Object Lock retention is designed to prevent deletion before the retention period.
explanations.b: Integrity retention controls must take precedence over ordinary lifecycle expiration for locked objects.
explanations.c: Integrity protection and encryption address different risks.
explanations.d: Object Lock preserves object versions and does not modify data.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.2: Design and configure mechanisms to protect data integrity.
questions.text: An application needs tamper-evident logs for incident investigations. What storage pattern fits?

answers.text: Logs stored only on mutable instance disks
Public delete access so teams can clean logs quickly
Centralized S3 log archive with versioning, Object Lock where required, and restricted delete access
No timestamps in log records

explanations.a: Instance-local logs can be altered or lost during compromise.
explanations.b: Broad delete access undermines integrity.
explanations.c: Tamper-evident log storage depends on protected versions, retention controls, and limited administrative access.
explanations.d: Timestamps are essential to integrity and investigation timelines.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.2: Design and configure mechanisms to protect data integrity.
questions.text: A signing key used for deployment artifacts is broadly accessible. What integrity risk exists?

answers.text: The artifacts automatically become larger
S3 Versioning stops working
CloudFront caches become encrypted
Unauthorized principals could sign untrusted artifacts as if they were approved

explanations.a: Key exposure affects trust, not artifact size.
explanations.b: Signing key access does not disable S3 Versioning.
explanations.c: Signing key exposure does not encrypt caches.
explanations.d: Code signing depends on protecting the signing key and limiting who can produce trusted signatures.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.2: Design and configure mechanisms to protect data integrity.
questions.text: A team must prove that retained records were not changed after ingestion. What evidence helps?

answers.text: Object Lock retention status, version IDs, audit logs, and checksum records
Only the bucket display name
Only monthly cost reports
Only a screenshot without version or timestamp data

explanations.a: Integrity proof needs retention metadata, immutable version references, access history, and content validation.
explanations.b: Bucket names do not prove records stayed unchanged.
explanations.c: Cost reports do not validate record integrity.
explanations.d: Screenshots without durable identifiers are weak integrity evidence.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.3: Design automatic lifecycle management and retention solutions for data.
questions.text: A data lake must keep raw logs for seven years and move older data to lower-cost storage. What should be configured?

answers.text: An ALB listener rule
S3 Lifecycle policies with retention aligned to compliance requirements
A security group egress rule
A Lambda memory setting

explanations.a: Listener rules route web traffic and do not manage data retention.
explanations.b: Lifecycle policies can transition and expire objects according to age and retention rules.
explanations.c: Network egress rules do not transition stored objects.
explanations.d: Function memory does not define long-term data retention.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.3: Design automatic lifecycle management and retention solutions for data.
questions.text: An EFS file system contains infrequently accessed reports. The team wants automatic cost optimization without deleting data. Which feature applies?

answers.text: S3 CORS configuration
AWS WAF rate limiting
EFS Lifecycle policies
KMS key rotation only

explanations.a: CORS controls browser access to S3 and not EFS file lifecycle.
explanations.b: WAF rate limiting does not manage file storage class.
explanations.c: EFS Lifecycle policies can move files to lower-cost storage classes based on access patterns.
explanations.d: Key rotation does not move EFS files between storage classes.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.3: Design automatic lifecycle management and retention solutions for data.
questions.text: A retention rule must prevent deletion for five years and then allow expiration. Which design fits?

answers.text: Immediate expiration with no retention lock
Indefinite retention for all data without review
Public write access to the archive bucket
Object Lock retention combined with lifecycle expiration after the retention period

explanations.a: Immediate deletion violates the retention requirement.
explanations.b: Indefinite storage may exceed policy or cost requirements.
explanations.c: Public writes do not implement lifecycle or retention control.
explanations.d: Retention controls protect data until the required period ends, and lifecycle can remove it afterward.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.3: Design automatic lifecycle management and retention solutions for data.
questions.text: A workload stores temporary processing files that must be deleted after 30 days. What should be used?

answers.text: Lifecycle expiration for the temporary object prefix
Manual console deletion once per year
S3 Object Lock compliance mode for the temporary prefix
A CloudFront response header policy

explanations.a: Prefix-specific lifecycle rules can delete short-lived data automatically.
explanations.b: Annual manual deletion is delayed and inconsistent.
explanations.c: Compliance retention would prevent deletion and conflicts with short-lived temporary data.
explanations.d: Response headers do not delete stored processing files.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.3: Design automatic lifecycle management and retention solutions for data.
questions.text: An FSx for Lustre file system needs backups retained according to policy. What should the design include?

answers.text: Only API Gateway stage variables
FSx backup policies with retention and restore testing
Only application comments describing backups
Only DNS failover records

explanations.a: Stage variables do not manage FSx backups.
explanations.b: Managed backups and validation align file system recovery points with retention requirements.
explanations.c: Comments do not create or retain backups.
explanations.d: DNS failover does not retain file system recovery points.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.3: Design automatic lifecycle management and retention solutions for data.
questions.text: A company wants to classify data before assigning lifecycle retention periods. What process should occur first?

answers.text: Apply the shortest retention to every dataset
Apply the longest retention to every dataset automatically
Identify data categories, legal requirements, access patterns, and recovery needs
Choose retention based only on bucket name length

explanations.a: Uniform short retention can violate legal and recovery requirements.
explanations.b: Uniform long retention can increase cost and data exposure.
explanations.c: Lifecycle design should be based on data value, obligations, and how often data is needed.
explanations.d: Name length does not represent legal or business requirements.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.3: Design automatic lifecycle management and retention solutions for data.
questions.text: A lifecycle rule transitions objects to archival storage, but analysts need frequent queries for the last 90 days. What design is appropriate?

answers.text: Archive all objects immediately after upload
Disable all lifecycle policies forever
Delete current partitions before analysis
Keep recent partitions in a frequently accessed class and transition older partitions later

explanations.a: Immediate archival storage can make current analysis slow or costly.
explanations.b: Removing lifecycle automation can increase cost and retention drift.
explanations.c: Deleting recent data would break investigation needs.
explanations.d: Lifecycle policies should match access patterns so current investigations remain efficient.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.3: Design automatic lifecycle management and retention solutions for data.
questions.text: A lifecycle policy expired evidence objects still under legal hold. What control was missing?

answers.text: Retention or legal hold controls that override ordinary expiration for scoped evidence
More aggressive expiration rules
A wider security group rule
A different ALB TLS policy

explanations.a: Legal retention needs explicit protection so normal lifecycle cleanup cannot remove held artifacts.
explanations.b: Faster expiration worsens legal hold risk.
explanations.c: Network access rules do not protect evidence retention.
explanations.d: TLS policy does not preserve evidence objects.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.3: Design automatic lifecycle management and retention solutions for data.
questions.text: A team wants lifecycle policies managed consistently across accounts. Which approach helps?

answers.text: Let every bucket owner manually invent retention rules
Deploy standardized lifecycle and retention configurations through infrastructure as code
Store lifecycle requirements only in email
Disable CloudTrail for lifecycle changes

explanations.a: Manual per-bucket decisions create inconsistency and audit gaps.
explanations.b: Codified lifecycle rules reduce drift and make retention behavior auditable across accounts.
explanations.c: Email does not enforce configuration.
explanations.d: Lifecycle changes should remain auditable.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.4: Design and configure secure data replication and backup solutions.
questions.text: A ransomware concern requires backups that workload administrators cannot delete. What design should be used?

answers.text: Keep backups only in the workload account with administrator delete access
Store backups only on the original instance
Copy backups to a separate backup account with locked vault retention
Disable backup logs to hide backup locations

explanations.a: Same-account broad delete rights can let attackers remove backups.
explanations.b: Instance-local backups can be encrypted or deleted by the same compromise.
explanations.c: Separate administration and locked retention reduce the chance that compromised workload access destroys recovery points.
explanations.d: Audit logs help verify backup and deletion activity.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.4: Design and configure secure data replication and backup solutions.
questions.text: A company must recover S3 data after accidental deletes in the primary Region. Which design supports this?

answers.text: A single current object version with no replication
Public write access to the destination bucket
Only a CloudWatch dashboard of object counts
S3 Versioning with replication and protected destination retention where required

explanations.a: One mutable version provides limited recovery after deletion or overwrite.
explanations.b: Public write access can corrupt or overwrite replicated data.
explanations.c: Visibility does not create recoverable copies.
explanations.d: Versioning and replication preserve recoverable copies outside the immediate delete path.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.4: Design and configure secure data replication and backup solutions.
questions.text: A workload uses AWS Backup across multiple services. What should be validated?

answers.text: Backup plans, vault access policies, restore testing, encryption, and cross-account or cross-Region copies
Only the display name of the vault
Only the number of running EC2 instances
Only an application release note

explanations.a: Secure backup design needs policy, protection, cryptographic controls, and proof that restores work.
explanations.b: Vault names do not prove recoverability or security.
explanations.c: Instance count does not validate backup coverage.
explanations.d: Release notes do not show backup success or restore capability.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.4: Design and configure secure data replication and backup solutions.
questions.text: A team needs to transfer protected data between accounts for migration while preserving encryption and auditability. Which service can help?

answers.text: Untracked manual download to laptops
AWS DataSync with scoped roles, encryption, and logging
Public bucket sharing during migration
Email attachments for bulk migration

explanations.a: Laptop transfers create uncontrolled copies and weak audit trails.
explanations.b: DataSync can move data between storage locations while using controlled permissions and operational logs.
explanations.c: Public access exposes data beyond the migration participants.
explanations.d: Email is not a secure or scalable data migration method.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.4: Design and configure secure data replication and backup solutions.
questions.text: A backup vault uses a KMS key that only one administrator can manage. What resilience issue exists?

answers.text: Backup objects automatically become unencrypted
Vault names become invalid
Recovery can fail if key access is unavailable or not granted to restore roles
Region routing tables stop working

explanations.a: Key governance affects access, not whether encryption existed.
explanations.b: Vault naming is not tied to administrator availability.
explanations.c: Encrypted backups require usable key permissions during restore, so key governance must support recovery.
explanations.d: KMS administrator access does not control network routing.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.4: Design and configure secure data replication and backup solutions.
questions.text: A disaster recovery plan includes cross-Region backup copies. What must also be tested?

answers.text: Only copying the runbook title
Only increasing source Region retention
Only changing DNS TTL values
Restore from the copied recovery points in the recovery Region

explanations.a: A title does not validate the restore path.
explanations.b: Source retention does not prove recovery Region usability.
explanations.c: DNS TTL changes do not restore encrypted data from backups.
explanations.d: Replication or copy success does not prove that recovery can be performed in the target Region.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.4: Design and configure secure data replication and backup solutions.
questions.text: A database backup is encrypted with a customer managed KMS key. What must be included in backup planning?

answers.text: KMS key policy and grants that allow authorized backup and restore operations
A public key policy for every principal
No encryption for backups to simplify restore
Only a lifecycle rule on application logs

explanations.a: Note that Secure replication and backup workflows rely on cryptographic authorization for both copy and restore.
explanations.b: Public decrypt access would expose protected backups.
explanations.c: Removing encryption weakens backup confidentiality.
explanations.d: Log lifecycle does not authorize encrypted database restores.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.4: Design and configure secure data replication and backup solutions.
questions.text: A security team wants to detect gaps in backup coverage. What should be monitored?

answers.text: Only weekly screenshots of the console
AWS Backup compliance reports, backup job status, protected resource assignments, and restore test results
Only the number of IAM users
Only VPC subnet route tables

explanations.a: Screenshots are stale and hard to aggregate.
explanations.b: Coverage monitoring should verify which resources are protected and whether jobs and restores succeed.
explanations.c: User count does not show backup coverage.
explanations.d: Route tables do not report backup protection status.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.2.4: Design and configure secure data replication and backup solutions.
questions.text: A backup strategy must protect against malicious deletion and accidental corruption. Which combination is strongest?

answers.text: One mutable backup in the same account
No backups because production is multi-AZ
Immutable retention, versioned copies, cross-account storage, and tested clean restores
Backups encrypted with an inaccessible key

explanations.a: A single mutable copy has limited protection from malicious or accidental changes.
explanations.b: High availability does not replace recoverable backups.
explanations.c: Layered backup controls preserve recovery points and validate that usable data can be restored.
explanations.d: Encryption is required, but unavailable keys can block recovery.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.1: Design management and rotation of credentials and secrets.
questions.text: A database password is stored in Secrets Manager and must rotate automatically. What should be configured?

answers.text: Hardcode the rotated password in source code
Email the secret to every operator after rotation
Store the password in an EC2 tag
Secrets Manager rotation with a supported integration or rotation Lambda

explanations.a: Hardcoded secrets are difficult to rotate and can leak through repositories.
explanations.b: Email distribution exposes credentials and is not controlled rotation.
explanations.c: Tags are metadata and not secure secret storage.
explanations.d: Secrets Manager can coordinate secret value updates and target credential rotation.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.1: Design management and rotation of credentials and secrets.
questions.text: A rotation Lambda changes a password but does not test it before completion. What should be added?

answers.text: A validation step that authenticates with the pending credential before finalizing rotation
A log statement that prints the password
Immediate deletion of the previous version before testing
A random delay with no connectivity test

explanations.a: Secret rotation should prove the new credential works before promoting it to current.
explanations.b: Printing secrets exposes them and does not safely validate use.
explanations.c: Removing rollback material before validation can cause outages.
explanations.d: Waiting does not prove the credential is valid.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.1: Design management and rotation of credentials and secrets.
questions.text: A service caches a secret for 24 hours and fails after rotation. What should be reviewed?

answers.text: Only the S3 bucket region
Application refresh behavior and secret cache TTL
Only the ALB cipher policy
Only the dashboard widget order

explanations.a: Bucket region does not explain stale credential caching.
explanations.b: Rotation requires applications to retrieve updated secret values or refresh cached credentials safely.
explanations.c: TLS cipher settings do not refresh application secrets.
explanations.d: Dashboard layout has no effect on cached credentials.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.1: Design management and rotation of credentials and secrets.
questions.text: A third-party API key is stored in Parameter Store as plaintext. The company requires encryption and controlled access. What should change?

answers.text: Place the API key in a public repository
Move the key into a log message for visibility
Store the value as a SecureString or secret with KMS protection and scoped IAM access
Use a security group rule as the key vault

explanations.a: Public source storage exposes the credential.
explanations.b: That logs should not contain secret values.
explanations.c: Secret values need encrypted storage and limited retrieval permissions.
explanations.d: Security groups do not store or protect secrets.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.1: Design management and rotation of credentials and secrets.
questions.text: An application needs database credentials at runtime. What pattern reduces credential exposure?

answers.text: Bake the database password into the container image
Store the password in a README
Give every workload access to every secret
Retrieve the secret at runtime using the workload role and least-privilege access

explanations.a: Image-baked secrets spread to every copy of the artifact.
explanations.b: Documentation files are not secret stores.
explanations.c: Broad secret access increases blast radius.
explanations.d: Runtime retrieval with a scoped role avoids baking secrets into images or code.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.1: Design management and rotation of credentials and secrets.
questions.text: A rotation policy requires emergency rollback to a previous secret version. What must be managed carefully?

answers.text: Version staging labels and retention of previous versions during the rollback window
Deleting all previous versions immediately after rotation
Publishing previous versions in chat
Using object storage class names for secret versions

explanations.a: Secrets Manager staging labels control which version applications retrieve and can support rollback when governed.
explanations.b: Immediate deletion removes rollback options.
explanations.c: Chat exposure compromises secret values.
explanations.d: Storage class names do not control secret staging labels.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.1: Design management and rotation of credentials and secrets.
questions.text: A security team wants to know who retrieved a sensitive secret. What should be enabled or reviewed?

answers.text: Only VPC subnet counts
CloudTrail events for Secrets Manager access and KMS decrypt activity
Only application logo updates
Only S3 CORS rules

explanations.a: Subnet counts do not show who accessed a secret.
explanations.b: Secret retrieval and key use produce audit evidence that can identify principals and timing.
explanations.c: Branding changes do not audit secret retrieval.
explanations.d: CORS rules do not record Secrets Manager access.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.1: Design management and rotation of credentials and secrets.
questions.text: A credential is shared by multiple applications and rotation causes outages. What design improvement is needed?

answers.text: Use one permanent credential for every application forever
Disable authentication between applications
Separate secrets by application or trust boundary with coordinated dependency updates
Store all secrets in one environment variable file on every host

explanations.a: Shared nonrotating credentials expand impact if compromised.
explanations.b: Removing authentication is not a rotation strategy.
explanations.c: Secret isolation reduces rotation blast radius and clarifies ownership.
explanations.d: Host-wide shared files increase exposure and coupling.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.1: Design management and rotation of credentials and secrets.
questions.text: A team must rotate secrets across accounts. What automation pattern is appropriate?

answers.text: Root credentials from every account in the rotation script
Manual copy and paste of secrets between consoles
Public secret replication for all accounts
Cross-account scoped rotation roles, centralized scheduling, and per-secret ownership metadata

explanations.a: Root credential storage is unsafe and unnecessary.
explanations.b: Manual copying is error-prone and exposes secret values.
explanations.c: Public sharing would compromise the secrets.
explanations.d: Multi-account secret rotation needs authorized paths, scheduling, and clear ownership to handle failures safely.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.2: Manage and use imported key material.
questions.text: A workload imports key material into a KMS key. What operational responsibility does the customer retain?

answers.text: Securely generating, importing, rotating, and reimporting key material before expiration or deletion
AWS automatically replaces expired imported material without customer action
The key becomes a public certificate
CloudTrail stops recording key use

explanations.a: Imported key material gives the customer responsibility for managing the external material lifecycle.
explanations.b: Imported key material requires customer lifecycle management.
explanations.c: KMS key material is not converted into a public TLS certificate.
explanations.d: KMS usage can still be audited through AWS logging.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.2: Manage and use imported key material.
questions.text: Imported key material is configured with an expiration time. What happens if it expires?

answers.text: The key automatically switches to AWS generated key material
Cryptographic operations that need the key material fail until material is reimported
All encrypted data is immediately deleted
Every IAM user gains decrypt access

explanations.a: Imported keys do not silently change material origin.
explanations.b: KMS cannot use expired imported key material for encryption or decryption operations.
explanations.c: Expiration blocks cryptographic use but does not delete ciphertext.
explanations.d: Expiration does not broaden authorization.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.2: Manage and use imported key material.
questions.text: A team wants to delete imported key material temporarily to make ciphertext inaccessible. What should they understand?

answers.text: Deleting imported material deletes all KMS audit events
Deleting imported material rotates the key automatically
Deleting imported material makes dependent decrypt operations unavailable until compatible material is reimported
Deleting imported material changes all IAM policies

explanations.a: Audit events remain separate evidence and are not removed by deleting material.
explanations.b: Deletion removes material; it is not a managed rotation process.
explanations.c: Removing imported material can be used to control availability of data encrypted under the key.
explanations.d: IAM policies are not rewritten by KMS material deletion.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.2: Manage and use imported key material.
questions.text: A company needs to rotate imported key material. What is a required planning point?

answers.text: Rotation removes the need for key policy review
Rotation can be performed by changing only the alias name
Rotation automatically publishes the material to every Region
Applications and data encrypted under old material may still require the original compatible material for decryption

explanations.a: Key policy governance remains required.
explanations.b: Aliases do not change cryptographic material.
explanations.c: Imported material must be managed according to the key and Region design.
explanations.d: Imported material rotation must preserve decryptability for existing ciphertext or re-encrypt data as designed.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.2: Manage and use imported key material.
questions.text: An external key store is used with KMS. What availability concern matters?

answers.text: KMS cryptographic operations depend on connectivity and availability of the external key store
External key stores remove all need for IAM authorization
External key stores make plaintext public by design
External key stores disable CloudTrail for KMS

explanations.a: External key stores place part of the cryptographic availability path outside the standard KMS key material boundary.
explanations.b: IAM and key policy authorization still apply.
explanations.c: External key stores control key material location and do not require public plaintext exposure.
explanations.d: KMS activity can still be logged.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.2: Manage and use imported key material.
questions.text: A security team imports key material from an on-premises HSM. What transfer requirement is important?

answers.text: Email the raw key material to an administrator
Protect the key material during import using the KMS import token and wrapping key process
Put raw key material in application logs
Store key material in public S3 for download

explanations.a: Emailing raw material exposes cryptographic secrets.
explanations.b: The import process is designed to protect key material while it is transferred to KMS.
explanations.c: This option logs must not contain cryptographic key material.
explanations.d: Public storage would compromise the key material.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.2: Manage and use imported key material.
questions.text: A KMS key with imported material is scheduled for deletion. What must be confirmed?

answers.text: The key alias will decrypt data after key deletion
IAM policies can decrypt ciphertext without KMS
No protected data still requires the key or a recovery plan exists before the waiting period completes
CloudFront cache entries preserve all decrypted data

explanations.a: Aliases point to keys and cannot decrypt without the key.
explanations.b: IAM authorizes requests but does not perform cryptographic operations.
explanations.c: Deleting a KMS key can make protected data unrecoverable if no alternative exists.
explanations.d: Cache entries are not a reliable data recovery plan.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.2: Manage and use imported key material.
questions.text: A multi-Region architecture uses imported key material. What must be designed per Region?

answers.text: Assume one Region's imported material automatically satisfies every Region
Use public DNS records as key material
Ignore Region-specific key policies
The key material import, availability, policy, and recovery process for each required Region

explanations.a: Regional key behavior must be validated for the multi-Region design.
explanations.b: DNS records are not cryptographic key material.
explanations.c: Key policies still determine who can use keys in each Region.
explanations.d: Imported material and regional cryptographic operations need explicit lifecycle planning in each Region used.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.2: Manage and use imported key material.
questions.text: Imported key material is used to satisfy a requirement for customer-origin key bytes. What evidence should be retained?

answers.text: Key material origin, import procedure records, expiration settings, key policies, and usage logs
Only a screenshot of a key alias
Only monthly storage costs
Only the number of encrypted objects

explanations.a: Evidence for imported key material should show provenance, lifecycle handling, authorization, and use.
explanations.b: An alias screenshot does not prove material origin or import procedure.
explanations.c: Cost reports do not prove key material governance.
explanations.d: Object count does not show how imported material was managed.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.3: Describe the differences between imported key material and AWS generated key material.
questions.keyword: Imported versus AWS generated key material
questions.text: A team compares KMS keys with AWS generated key material and imported key material. What is a key difference?

answers.text: Imported key material is always public
AWS generated key material is created and managed by KMS, while imported key material is supplied and lifecycle-managed by the customer
AWS generated key material cannot be used for encryption
Imported key material removes all key policies

explanations.a: Imported key material remains secret and must be protected by the customer and KMS import process.
explanations.b: The key material origin changes who manages generation and lifecycle responsibilities.
explanations.c: AWS generated key material is commonly used for KMS encryption operations.
explanations.d: KMS keys still use policies regardless of material origin.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.3: Describe the differences between imported key material and AWS generated key material.
questions.keyword: Imported versus AWS generated key material
questions.text: A company wants automatic KMS key rotation with minimal lifecycle burden. Which material origin is simpler?

answers.text: Imported key material with no rotation plan
Raw symmetric keys stored in application code
AWS generated key material
TLS certificates stored as KMS key aliases

explanations.a: Imported material requires customer-managed lifecycle and rotation planning.
explanations.b: Application-stored keys increase exposure and management burden.
explanations.c: KMS can manage automatic rotation for eligible keys with AWS generated key material.
explanations.d: Aliases are not certificate or key material lifecycle automation.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.3: Describe the differences between imported key material and AWS generated key material.
questions.keyword: Imported versus AWS generated key material
questions.text: A requirement states the organization must be able to remove key material from KMS to make data temporarily inaccessible. Which origin supports this pattern?

answers.text: AWS generated key material with no deletion of the key
An IAM policy condition only
A CloudWatch alarm
Imported key material

explanations.a: AWS generated material cannot be selectively removed while keeping the key object in the same way.
explanations.b: Policy changes can deny access but do not remove cryptographic material.
explanations.c: Alarms detect conditions and do not control key material presence.
explanations.d: Imported key material can be deleted from KMS and reimported if the lifecycle is managed correctly.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.3: Describe the differences between imported key material and AWS generated key material.
questions.keyword: Imported versus AWS generated key material
questions.text: A team assumes imported key material is safer because AWS never participates in encryption. What correction is needed?

answers.text: KMS still performs cryptographic operations; imported material changes key origin and lifecycle responsibility
Imported key material means data is never encrypted
Imported key material disables all audit logs
Imported key material turns the key into a password

explanations.a: Imported material does not bypass KMS operations or authorization controls.
explanations.b: Imported material is used for encryption and decryption operations.
explanations.c: KMS API use can still be logged.
explanations.d: KMS keys are cryptographic keys, not login passwords.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.3: Describe the differences between imported key material and AWS generated key material.
questions.keyword: Imported versus AWS generated key material
questions.text: A workload requires FIPS-validated managed key service without customer handling raw key bytes. Which option usually fits?

answers.text: Imported raw key material emailed between administrators
AWS generated KMS key material in AWS KMS
Plaintext keys inside application configuration files
Public S3 objects containing key bytes

explanations.a: Email handling of raw keys creates serious exposure risk.
explanations.b: AWS generated material avoids customer raw-key handling while using the managed KMS service.
explanations.c: Application configuration is not a managed key service.
explanations.d: Public storage of keys would compromise encrypted data.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.3: Describe the differences between imported key material and AWS generated key material.
questions.keyword: Imported versus AWS generated key material
questions.text: A key with imported material expires and decrypt operations fail. Would an AWS generated key have the same expiration behavior for material?

answers.text: Yes; all KMS key material expires every day
Yes; expiration always grants decrypt to everyone
No; AWS generated key material does not use the customer-defined imported material expiration setting
No; AWS generated keys cannot decrypt anything

explanations.a: AWS generated key material does not expire through imported-material expiration settings.
explanations.b: Expiration does not grant access.
explanations.c: Imported material can have expiration behavior that requires customer reimport planning.
explanations.d: AWS generated keys can perform decrypt operations when authorized.

questions.name: Data Protection

questions.keyword: Imported versus AWS generated key material
questions.text: A risk review compares operational burden for imported and AWS generated key material. Which statement is accurate?

answers.text: Imported material eliminates the need for backups or recovery planning
AWS generated material requires customers to store raw key bytes
Both origins remove IAM evaluation
Imported material adds customer responsibilities for generation, storage, reimport, and recovery planning

explanations.a: Imported material increases the need for careful recovery planning.
explanations.b: KMS manages AWS generated key material and customers do not handle raw bytes.
explanations.c: Authorization still applies to KMS requests.
explanations.d: Customer-supplied material creates lifecycle tasks beyond ordinary managed key policy administration.
