questions.text: A compliance team asks how material origin affects evidence. What evidence differs for imported material?

answers.text: Records showing customer key generation, wrapping, import, expiration, and reimport procedures
Only proof that the key has any alias
Only proof that an S3 bucket exists
Only proof of ALB TLS settings

explanations.a: Imported material requires evidence of customer-controlled material lifecycle steps.
explanations.b: Aliases do not prove origin-specific lifecycle control.
explanations.c: Bucket existence does not show KMS material origin.
explanations.d: ALB TLS configuration does not document KMS key material origin.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.3: Describe the differences between imported key material and AWS generated key material.
questions.keyword: Imported versus AWS generated key material
questions.text: A company wants to avoid accidental data loss from losing external key bytes. Which material origin reduces that specific risk?

answers.text: Imported material with no retained copy
AWS generated key material
Keys stored only in build logs
One plaintext key shared in email

explanations.a: Losing imported material can make reimport or recovery impossible.
explanations.b: With AWS generated material, KMS manages key material durability and customers do not need to preserve external key bytes for reimport.
explanations.c: That logs are not safe key custody.
explanations.d: Email custody is insecure and fragile.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.4: Mask sensitive data.
questions.text: Application logs contain credit card numbers in CloudWatch Logs. What control should be applied?

answers.text: Increase log retention forever
Make the log group public for review
CloudWatch Logs data protection policy to audit or mask sensitive patterns
Disable TLS on log ingestion

explanations.a: Longer retention preserves the exposed data rather than masking it.
explanations.b: Public log access would spread the sensitive data.
explanations.c: CloudWatch Logs data protection policies can detect and mask sensitive data in log events.
explanations.d: Plaintext transport would increase exposure and does not mask data.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.4: Mask sensitive data.
questions.text: SNS messages may include accidental PII. Which feature helps prevent exposure to subscribers?

answers.text: SNS topic display names only
A VPC route table entry
S3 Versioning for unrelated logs
Amazon SNS message data protection

explanations.a: Display names do not inspect or mask message content.
explanations.b: Routing does not mask sensitive message payloads.
explanations.c: Versioning does not protect SNS message contents.
explanations.d: SNS message data protection can audit, de-identify, or protect sensitive data in message payloads.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.4: Mask sensitive data.
questions.text: A support dashboard should show partial identifiers without revealing full account numbers. What masking approach fits?

answers.text: Tokenize or redact sensitive portions while preserving non-sensitive context needed for support
Show full identifiers to every support user
Remove all context including the case reference
Store identifiers only in dashboard titles

explanations.a: Masking should reduce exposure while keeping enough information for authorized workflows.
explanations.b: Broad full-value display increases unnecessary sensitive data exposure.
explanations.c: Over-redaction can make legitimate support work impossible.
explanations.d: Titles do not provide controlled masking.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.4: Mask sensitive data.
questions.text: A developer wants to print full Secrets Manager values during troubleshooting. What should be done instead?

answers.text: Print the full secret and delete it later
Log secret identifiers or validation status, not the secret value
Send the secret through an unencrypted chat channel
Disable all application authentication

explanations.a: This pattern logs may be replicated, retained, or accessed before deletion.
explanations.b: In this scenario, Sensitive data masking requires diagnostic logs to avoid exposing credential material.
explanations.c: Chat exposure spreads the credential outside controlled storage.
explanations.d: Authentication removal does not provide safe troubleshooting.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.4: Mask sensitive data.
questions.text: A company wants to detect national identifiers in log streams and generate findings without breaking applications. What mode should be considered first?

answers.text: Immediate deletion of all log streams
Public posting of detected identifiers
Audit mode for sensitive data findings before enforcing masking or blocking behavior
Disabling all detection to avoid findings

explanations.a: Deleting logs removes operational evidence.
explanations.b: Public disclosure worsens sensitive data exposure.
explanations.c: Audit-first deployment helps assess impact and tune sensitive data masking controls safely.
explanations.d: Removing detection leaves the exposure unknown.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.4: Mask sensitive data.
questions.text: A masking control hides values in CloudWatch Logs, but raw payloads are also stored in S3. What gap remains?

answers.text: CloudWatch masking automatically rewrites every S3 object
S3 objects cannot contain sensitive data
Encryption at rest removes the need for minimization
Sensitive data must also be protected or redacted in the S3 storage path

explanations.a: Log data protection policies do not automatically sanitize unrelated S3 payloads.
explanations.b: S3 commonly stores sensitive data and must be governed.
explanations.c: Encryption protects storage but authorized readers could still see raw sensitive values.
explanations.d: Masking one telemetry destination does not protect copies stored elsewhere.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.4: Mask sensitive data.
questions.text: A centralized logging platform receives JSON events with customer emails. What design improves masking accuracy?

answers.text: Use consistent structured fields and data protection rules for known sensitive attributes
Randomize field names for every service
Store emails in multiple free-form fields intentionally
Remove all timestamps from events

explanations.a: Structured field names help sensitive data controls target values without damaging unrelated text.
explanations.b: Inconsistent fields make masking and queries harder.
explanations.c: Scattered free-form values are harder to protect accurately.
explanations.d: Timestamps support investigations and are unrelated to masking accuracy.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.4: Mask sensitive data.
questions.text: A notification includes an access token in an SNS message. What is the safest response?

answers.text: Leave the token active because SNS is managed
Treat the token as exposed, rotate or revoke it, and update message data protection controls
Forward the message to more channels for awareness
Only rename the SNS topic

explanations.a: Managed messaging does not make exposed tokens safe.
explanations.b: Here, Sensitive data masking failures involving tokens require credential containment and prevention updates.
explanations.c: More forwarding spreads the token.
explanations.d: Renaming the topic does not invalidate the exposed token.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.4: Mask sensitive data.
questions.text: A privacy team wants evidence that masking controls are working. What should be collected?

answers.text: Only the number of log groups
Only a verbal statement from developers
Data protection policy configuration, audit findings, sample redacted outputs, and access logs
Only the S3 storage class of logs

explanations.a: Log group count does not prove masking effectiveness.
explanations.b: Verbal confirmation is weak compared with configuration and sample evidence.
explanations.c: Evidence should prove both configuration and observed masking behavior while showing who accessed protected data.
explanations.d: Storage class does not show whether sensitive fields are masked.

questions.name: Data Protection

questions.text: A global application encrypts data in two Regions and needs a related key in each Region for failover. What should be considered?

answers.text: One single-Region key alias reused by name everywhere
A public KMS key policy for all Regions
Only CloudFront geographic restrictions
AWS KMS multi-Region keys with policies and grants configured for each Region

explanations.a: Alias name reuse does not make a key available in another Region.
explanations.b: Public cryptographic access would expose protected data.
explanations.c: Geographic restrictions do not create regional encryption keys.
explanations.d: Multi-Region keys can support regional encryption and decryption patterns when each replica is governed correctly.

Only a global dashboard title

answers.text: No policies because replicas trust everyone
Only matching alias names
Appropriate key policies and grants on the primary and replica keys
Only DNS records for key IDs

explanations.a: KMS keys still require authorization policies.
explanations.b: Aliases do not grant access.
explanations.c: Multi-Region key relationship does not automatically grant every principal access in every Region.
explanations.d: DNS does not authorize KMS operations.

questions.name: Data Protection
questions.objective: Skill 5.3.5: Create and manage encryption keys and certificates across a single AWS Region or multiple Regions.
questions.text: A company wants consistent key and certificate provisioning across accounts. What approach is appropriate?

answers.text: Manual console creation with no standards
Shared private keys copied through chat
Disable all certificate validation
Use infrastructure as code with approved key policies, certificate validation, and rotation or renewal workflows

explanations.a: Manual unmanaged creation leads to drift and missed renewal paths.
explanations.b: Private keys must not be distributed through chat.
explanations.c: Validation is required to prove domain or private trust ownership.
explanations.d: Codified key and certificate management reduces drift and provides reviewable governance across environments.
